question: In which of the following states is the festival Vishu celebrated?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Kerala**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Vishu is an important festival in the state of **Kerala**, celebrated with great enthusiasm and joy.
 
• It marks the beginning of the Malayalam New Year and is observed in the month of April.
 
• The festival is known for the ritual of 'Vishukkani,' which means "the first thing seen on Vishu."
 
• Traditional customs include lighting lamps and seeing auspicious items like rice, fruits, and flowers first thing in the morning.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Vishu**

 
 
• Vishu is one of the major festivals celebrated in Kerala and parts of Tamil Nadu. It is similar to the festival of Baisakhi in Punjab, Puthandu in Tamil Nadu, and Bihu in Assam.
 
• The festival is characterized by the ritualistic arrangement of ‘Vishukkani,’ which includes items like rice, lemon, cucumber, coconut, jackfruit, kanikkonna (golden shower flower), betel leaves, areca nut, metal mirror, and coins.
 
• Another significant aspect of Vishu is the 'Vishukkaineetam,' where elders of the family give money to the younger members as a token of blessings.
 
• A special feast called 'Sadya' is prepared on this day, featuring a variety of traditional dishes served on a banana leaf.
 
 
 
• **Malayalam Calendar**
 
 
• The Malayalam calendar, also known as Kollavarsham, is a solar calendar used in Kerala. Vishu marks the first day of Medam, the ninth month of the Malayalam calendar.
 
• This calendar is used for various religious, cultural, and agricultural purposes in Kerala.
 
 
 
• **Vishukkani**
 
 
• The term 'Vishukkani' literally means the first sight on Vishu day. It is a traditional arrangement of auspicious items meant to be viewed first thing in the morning to bring prosperity and good luck.
 
• The arrangement is usually done the night before Vishu, and family members view it early in the morning, often with closed eyes until they reach the spot where the Vishukkani is set up.
 
 
 
• **Vishukkaineetam**
 
 
• Vishukkaineetam is a custom where elders give money to younger members of the family and other dependents. This is considered a gesture of blessing and goodwill.
 
• It is believed that receiving Vishukkaineetam brings prosperity and luck for the entire year.
